_about: The reviewed record behind the privacy policy. Everything under 'derived' is read back from the code by privacy/derive.py and compared by tests/test_privacy_policy.py: when the code moves away from this record, review the policy, then update this file and privacy.html together. See README.md.

backend.getlumina.pro.why: our server: the app's API and the extension's connection

api.typesafe.ai.why: the model that decides each browser step (JEV): gets a screenshot of the page and the task text with personal data removed

openrouter.ai.why: the experimental browser decider, limited in code to the owner's own account

api.stripe.com.why: payments; not in use while access is free

api.telegram.org.why: optional account linking; not configured on the live server (2026-10-31)

www.googleapis.com.why: connectors (Gmail, Calendar, Drive); switched off on the live server (2026-10-31)

app.asana.com.why: OAuth discovery, sign-in and token exchange for the optional customer-selected Asana MCP connection

mcp.asana.com.why: customer-selected Asana MCP tools and their authorized arguments

cdn.jsdelivr.net.why: Browser Python runtime download when a customer explicitly runs a Python delivery; receives client IP and download metadata.

recipients_not_visible_in_code.Anthropic: the assistant's model; every model in the server's LiteLLM config is anthropic/* (/opt/openclaw-production/config/litellm.yaml, checked 2026-10-31)
recipients_not_visible_in_code.Vercel: serves getlumina.pro and forwards requests to our server (platform/deploy/vercel)
recipients_not_visible_in_code.server hosting provider: the VPS the service runs on
recipients_not_visible_in_code.Brave Search: receives the assistant's web-search terms (the Brave plugin, a shared key held by the host: lifecycle/cell_config.py setup_search)
recipients_not_visible_in_code.Cloudflare: public DNS 1.1.1.1 used by the assistant's cell to look up website names (lifecycle/cell_config.py RESOLVERS)

policy_must_say: until you ask us to delete
This is everything we collect today
company that runs the endpoint you enter
Allow Lumina to use this tab
optional permission to read all sites

review_log.by: side-panel chat (written by Claude Code for the owner to review; not yet published)
review_log.note: The extension gains the sidePanel permission and one HTTPS call to Lumina's own server (https://backend.getlumina.pro/v1/panel, same host as the device link) for the side chat; it keeps the short-lived pass in memory only, plus one more developer-only setting (panelApi). chat_messages gains a nullable surface column holding only the label 'panel' (no personal data; the typed text already lives in the same table as every chat message). review_log.by: long-term memory (Hindsight), written by Claude Code for the owner to review; not yet published
review_log.note: New table longterm_memories: the plain text of short notes the assistant saved for a customer (preference/fact, one sentence, secrets refused), per account, visible and deletable by the customer, never restored from backups (LIVE in ops/restore.py). Notes are also indexed in a self-hosted Hindsight server (one bank per account, bank id = keyed hash computed on the server, never chosen by the assistant), configured with retain_extraction_mode=chunks and observations off, so it stores each note verbatim, calls no language model on notes and derives no text from them; embeddings and reranking must run locally on the same server (deploy/LONG_TERM_MEMORY.md). No new third party receives notes. Policy updated: short version, collect list, recipients (our memory service, same server), retention row, choices. Feature stays off (long-term-memory.json) until this policy is published and Hindsight is deployed per deploy/LONG_TERM_MEMORY.md.

review_log.by: owner goal: the extension becomes a standalone side chat like other assistants' extensions
review_log.note: New permissions tabs, scripting, contextMenus and an OPTIONAL all-sites permission asked for only inside the side chat. New behaviours the policy now states: the side chat opens on any tab and every open is a new session (a new chat titled "Browser extension", the assistant woken); the extension signs in to /v1/panel/session with its own device token; Lumina can work in a tab of the customer's own Chrome only after they press Allow on it (attached while a task runs, released after, never closed); tab names/addresses are sent only with a message that involves a tab; selected text (4,000) and page text (20,000) are sent only after the customer allows reading pages and are kept with the chat message; saved prompts and panel settings stay on the computer; the popup is gone (controls moved into the side chat). Checked against code: derive.py output, panel.py clean_context, browse/extension tests. Publish the page after merge.
